children.value: This section contains documentation of several sets of parameters that characterize responses to a tax reform. Consumption parameters are used to compute marginal tax rates and to compute the consumption value of in-kind benefits. Growdiff parameters are used to specify baseline differences and/or reform responses in the annual rate of growth in economic variables.

The assumption parameters control advanced features of Tax-Calculator, so understanding the source code that uses them is essential. Default values of many assumption parameters are zero and are projected into the future at that value, which implies no response to the reform. The benefit value consumption parameters have a default value of one, which implies the consumption value of the in-kind benefits is equal to the government cost of providing the benefits.

Default projection is in growfactors.csv file.  ABOOK extrapolates input variables: e07300 and e07400.

Default projection is in growfactors.csv file.  AWAGE extrapolates input variables: e00200, e00200p, e00200s, overtime_income, and tip_income. Note that non-zero values of this parameter will not affect historically known values of _SS_Earnings_c.

Marginal propensity to consume medical expenses
Defined as dollar change in medical-expense consumption divided by dollar change in income.  Typical value is in [0,1] range.
Marginal propensity to consume state-and-local taxes
Defined as dollar change in state-and-local-taxes consumption divided by dollar change in income.  Typical value is in [0,1] range.
Marginal propensity to consume charity cash contributions
Defined as dollar change in charity-cash-contribution consumption divided by dollar change in income.  Typical value is in [0,1] range.
Marginal propensity to consume miscellaneous deduction expenses
Defined as dollar change in miscellaneous-deduction-expense consumption divided by dollar change in income.  Typical value is in [0,1] range.
Consumption value per dollar of housing benefits, all of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of SNAP benefits, all of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of TANF benefits, some of which are cash benefits and some of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of veterans benefits, some of which are in-kind benefits (only about 48% are cash benefits).
Consumption value per dollar of WIC benefits, all of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of Medicare benefits, all of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of Medicaid benefits, all of which are in-kind benefits.
Consumption value per dollar of other benefits, some of which are in-kind benefits (somewhere between 52% and 76% are in-kind benefits).
